rationale: The opening step was exactly right (unplug, check filter and spray arms) and the customer found and cleared the real blockage. The assistant then fixated on residual upper-arm stiffness, headlining 'Likely cause: spray arm bearing' and asking for a model number 'to find the exact replacement part if this bearing is worn out', which the ground truth marks as not justified; the replacement-part panel was re-shown even after the customer declined. It never asked about programme choice, salt/rinse aid or scraping plates, and never told the customer to run a normal/hot programme to confirm the fix, so the aggravating factors in the hidden truth were missed.
